response.overview: This film "Baseball vs. Drugs" (1972) presents Major League Baseball’s campaign against drug abuse, launched in 1970 under Commissioner Bowie Kuhn. Featuring players like Reggie Smith and Wes Parker alongside medical experts, the film promotes dialogue about the dangers of drugs such as marijuana, amphetamines, barbiturates, and LSD. Here, athletes explain how addiction destroys health, focus, and self-control, countering the myth that drugs can enhance performance. True athletic success comes from discipline and hard work, not chemical shortcuts. The film concludes by reaffirming baseball’s zero-tolerance stance and its role as a national leader in promoting a drug-free lifestyle.
response.title: Baseball vs Drugs
